newsitem.title: FINLAND: Mixed Helsinki ends lower ahead of Nokia 96 report.
newsitem.headline: Mixed Helsinki ends lower ahead of Nokia 96 report.

text.p: Shares eased on Wednesday in a mixed session ahead of Nokia's trend-setting 1996 report due on Thursday, with Merita falling after in-line results and Rauma and Konecranes leading engineering stocks higher, brokers said.
The HEX closed 730 million markka trade off 0.08 percent at 2,835.3 points, with 46 advancing issues and 42 decliners.
Bourse engine Nokia inched down 1.00 to 323.00 markka, with relatively subdued trading interest which gave it only a third of bourse volume.
Finland's largest banking group Merita Oy suffered from profit-taking after it reported a 1.20 billion markka operating profit, up from 491 a year earlier.

UPM-Kymmene dragged forestries lower, correcting gains on Tuesday which followed an announcement that it would up LWC paper prices soon. UPM trimmed Tuesday's 2.70 markka gain by 0.70 to end lively trade at 99.50 markka.
Metsa-Serla was also lively but bucked the trend and ended 0.80 markka or over two percent higher at 38.40.
Sentra plunged 40 markka to 280.00 in a correction to dizzying over 80 percent gains on Monday and Tuesday.
A $50 million order helped engineering group Rauma add 4.50 markka to a new 113.00 markka year-high, just one markka below its record close and four below its all-time peak.
"Tomorrow we will first wait for Nokia report and then start shooting," one broker said, adding he expected volatility.
Nokia's 1996 report is due around 1300/1100 GMT.
The median forecast for Nokia's 1996 profit is 3.85 billion markka, down from a reported 4.93 billion in 1995.
